verdicts.name: CodeGraph
verdicts.summary: Maps your whole codebase so AI assistants understand how files connect.
verdicts.why: It uses Tree-sitter, a real code parser, instead of AI calls, so indexing is fast and predictable.
verdicts.best_for: projects big enough that your AI assistant keeps losing track of files.

verdicts.name: Graphify
verdicts.summary: Builds a map of your code, images and documents for your AI assistant.
verdicts.why: Genuinely helpful context, but it spends API tokens, so the bill grows with project size.
verdicts.best_for: small projects. For big codebases, CodeGraph is the cheaper choice.

verdicts.name: ManimCat
verdicts.summary: Turns plain-language requests into math animations.
verdicts.why: It checks and auto-fixes generated Python before running it, which is clever. But each output takes 15 to 90 seconds, and it depends on Redis and Bull, which makes serverless hosting hard.
verdicts.best_for: trying locally for fun. Not ready to build a product on yet.

verdicts.name: RAG-Anything
verdicts.summary: Ask questions over PDFs, images, tables and formulas together.
verdicts.why: Powerful, but it's a heavy framework built on LightRAG and MinerU, not a simple building block. Beginners will get lost.
verdicts.best_for: after you've built a plain text RAG app and understand how it works.

verdicts.name: Anti-detect browsers
verdicts.summary: Modified browsers that hide automation from websites' bot checks.
verdicts.why: They're trending with AI agents, but their main job is getting around website protections. That easily breaks a site's terms of service.
verdicts.best_for: use official APIs, or test browser automation on your own site.
